ruling.reasoning:
The trip ran 11.7 km against an optimal 9.8 km (+1.9 km) [F1], and the billed excess is 1.88 km at $1.4104/km = $2.65 [F4]. The single off-route segment 10:06–10:11 added 1.71 km over the optimal stretch and drove EDGEDALE PLAINS → PUNGGOL FIELD → PUNGGOL EAST → PUNGGOL CENTRAL → PASIR RIS INDUSTRIAL DRIVE 1 → HALUS LINK [F3]. The only question that moves the amount is the RD-5 notice-and-consent reading for that segment [F3][RD-5].

The rider gave prior consent: the call log shows a 40-second answered call at 09:56, before the 10:06 segment, in which the driver asked "ok if I go round via Halus Link?" and the rider answered "Ok, can, go ahead" [F8]. That is a rider acknowledgement before the point of deviation by the recorded-call route RD-5 requires, and the recording transcript — not the driver's later statement [F9] — is what establishes it [F8][RD-5]. The words name a road, HALUS LINK, which is among the roads this segment drove [F3], so the agreement is tied to the segment: the roads before and after HALUS LINK are part of going via Halus Link [F3][RD-5].

A traffic reason exists on the replaced stretch — the 09:47 accident 0 m from the optimal route on the Tampines Expressway, with band-1 congestion on that expressway during 09:50–10:11 [F13][F10] — so the informed-and-agreed branch of RD-2 applies and no driver violation is recorded; no RD-7 reminder is due [RD-4][RD-2]. The segment is exempt, leaving 1.88 km − 1.71 km = 0.17 km, which is within the 1 km tolerance; the trace therefore returns no_action [F3][RD-1][RD-2]. The $27.10 metered total includes base, distance, time, platform components with no surge in play [F6][F5], and nothing in it is refundable.

The record is complete for this ruling: GPS distance and segment breakdown [F1][F3], a timestamped call log with transcript [F8], traffic data [F10][F13], and the fare breakdown [F6]; the chat itself being empty [F7] does not leave an element undecidable because the recorded call supplies the consent [F8][RD-5].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, the driver's statement, the chat record and the call transcript [F7][F8][F9]. The only complaint is about the fare; there is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so no safety escalation arises [SAFE-1].

Precedent alignment: DISP-2026-0089 (uninformed reroute, $3.20) is distinguishable — there the rider was never informed, whereas here the rider agreed on a recorded call before the segment [F8][RD-5].
